examples.ko: 가스통이 너무 무거워서 혼자 못 들어요.
examples.en: The gas cylinder is too heavy for me to lift alone.

examples.ko: 이사할 때 가스통은 따로 옮겨야 해요.
examples.en: When you move, the gas cylinder has to be carried separately.
There is almost no gas left in the gas cylinder.
We swapped the restaurant's gas cylinder for a new one.

examples.ko: 가스통 옆에서는 불을 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not use fire next to a gas cylinder.
The man also delivered the gas cylinder in the morning.

explain: 도시가스가 없는 집, 식당, 캠핑장에서 연료로 쓰는 통을 말해요. '가스통을 갈다', '가스통을 배달시키다'처럼 자주 말해요. 뉴스에서는 폭발 사고와 함께 나오기도 해서 안전 이야기에도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the tank of fuel used in homes without city gas, in restaurants and at campsites. People often say '가스통을 갈다' (change the cylinder) or '가스통을 배달시키다' (order a delivery). It also appears in news about explosion accidents and safety.

examples.en: The child buried his face in his dad's chest.

examples.ko: 가슴팍이 넓어서 그 셔츠가 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: He has a broad chest, so that shirt suits him well.
I spilled coffee and my whole chest got wet.
Try walking with your chest pushed out.
The T-shirt has a big logo on the chest.
The puppy jumped all the way up to my chest.

explain: '가슴'보다 겉에서 보이는 앞쪽 넓은 부분, 특히 옷이 닿는 부분을 말할 때 많이 써요. 마음이나 감정을 말할 때는 '가슴'을 쓰고 '가슴팍'은 쓰지 않아요. 주로 남자의 몸이나 옷 이야기에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Compared with '가슴', it points to the broad front area of the body as seen from outside, especially where clothes sit. For feelings you use '가슴', not '가슴팍'. It is often heard when talking about a man's body or clothing.

examples.en: Visible light is light that human eyes can see.
A rainbow forms when visible light splits apart.
We learned about the colors of visible light in science class.
Ultraviolet rays have a shorter wavelength than visible light.

examples.ko: 이 카메라는 가시광선 말고 적외선도 찍어요.
examples.en: This camera captures infrared as well as visible light.

examples.ko: 가시광선에는 빨강부터 보라까지 여러 색이 있어요.
examples.en: Visible light contains many colors, from red to violet.

explain: 과학 수업과 시험에서 주로 나오는 말이에요. 눈에 안 보이는 '자외선', '적외선'과 짝으로 같이 배워요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '빛'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in science classes and exams. It is learned together with the invisible '자외선' (ultraviolet) and '적외선' (infrared). In everyday talk people just say '빛' (light).

examples.en: That person's life was a thorny path.
After walking a thorny path, he finally succeeded.
The road of a new actor is a thorny one.
I got through a time that felt like a thorny path.
Everyone says starting a business is a thorny road.

examples.ko: 가시밭길에도 함께 가는 친구가 있어서 힘이 났어요.
examples.en: Even on a thorny path, I had a friend beside me and felt strong.

explain: 진짜 가시가 있는 길보다 힘들고 어려운 삶이나 과정을 비유할 때 훨씬 많이 써요. '가시밭길을 걷다'가 가장 자연스러운 짝이에요. 반대로 쉽고 편한 길은 '꽃길'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used far more as a metaphor for a hard life or process than for a path with real thorns. '가시밭길을 걷다' is the most natural pairing. The opposite, an easy and happy road, is '꽃길'.

examples.ko: 올해 안에 개발 효과가 가시화될 거예요.
examples.en: The effects of the development will become visible within this year.

examples.ko: 새 계획의 성과가 슬슬 가시화되고 있어요.
examples.en: The results of the new plan are gradually becoming visible.

examples.ko: 문제가 가시화되기 전에 미리 준비해야 해요.
examples.en: We should prepare before the problem becomes apparent.
The cooperation between the two companies has finally taken concrete shape.
I'm worried because the change hasn't become visible yet.

examples.ko: 팀장님, 결과가 가시화되면 바로 알려 드릴게요.
examples.en: Team leader, I'll let you know right away when the results become visible.

explain: 눈에 보이지 않던 것이 겉으로 드러나기 시작한다는 느낌이라, 계획·성과·문제처럼 추상적인 것에 많이 써요. '실현되다'처럼 완전히 이루어진 것은 아니고, 모습이 보이기 시작한 단계예요. 회의나 뉴스에서 자주 들리는 편이고, 일상 대화에서는 '눈에 보이다'나 '드러나다'를 써요.
explain_en: It means something unseen starts to show on the surface, so it is often used for abstract things like plans, results, or problems. Unlike '실현되다' (to be realized), it is not fully achieved yet; it has just begun to take visible shape. You hear it in meetings and news, while everyday talk uses '눈에 보이다' or '드러나다'.

examples.en: That rumor became the gossip topic at the company.
Celebrity weddings are always gossip material.
Please don't make me into gossip.
All we talked about at lunch was gossip.
Something like this doesn't end as mere gossip.
I don't want to become gossip among my friends.

explain: '입방아에 오르다'와 비슷하게, 사람들이 재미로 말하는 소문이나 남의 사생활 이야기를 가리켜요. 보통 좋지 않은 느낌이라 '가십거리가 되다'는 남의 입에 오르내린다는 말이에요. 중립적인 '이야깃거리'와 달라요.
explain_en: Like '입방아에 오르다', it refers to rumors or other people's private lives that people talk about for fun. It usually has a negative feel, so '가십거리가 되다' means to become the subject of people's talk. It differs from the neutral '이야깃거리' (a topic to talk about).

examples.en: The puppy standing in the rain is so pitiful.
The child left alone looked pitiful.

examples.ko: 가여운 사람을 보면 그냥 못 지나가요.
examples.en: I can't just walk past someone who looks pitiful.

examples.ko: 아픈 동생이 가여워서 밤새 옆에 있었어요.
examples.en: I felt so sorry for my sick younger sibling that I stayed by their side all night.

examples.ko: 가엾다고 해서 다 도와줄 수는 없어요.
examples.en: Feeling sorry for someone doesn't mean I can help everyone.
That child's situation was truly pitiful.

explain: 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '가여워요', '가여운', '가여웠어요'가 돼요. '가엾다'도 같은 말인데 '가엾어요'처럼 규칙으로 활용해요. '불쌍하다'와 비슷하지만 '가엽다'는 마음이 아픈 느낌이 더 부드러워요.
explain_en: It is a 'ㅂ' irregular word, giving '가여워요', '가여운' and '가여웠어요'. '가엾다' is the same word and conjugates regularly, as in '가엾어요'. It is close to '불쌍하다', but '가엽다' feels a little softer and more tender.

examples.en: The child is clumsy at cutting with scissors.
The hairdresser's scissor work is really fast.
Please be careful when you cut with scissors.
Cut it out with scissors following the paper's shape.
I keep hearing the sound of scissors snipping.
I cut lots of paper to practice using scissors.

explain: 가위로 자르는 동작 자체를 말해요. '-질'은 어떤 도구로 하는 행동 뒤에 붙어요(삽질, 칼질처럼). 영상이나 기사의 '가위질'은 비유로 내용을 잘라 내는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the act of cutting with scissors itself. The suffix '-질' attaches to actions done with a tool, as in 삽질 and 칼질. In media talk, '가위질' is also used figuratively for cutting out content.

examples.en: I cut the colored paper into shapes with scissors.
The child cut his own bangs with scissors.

examples.ko: 천을 가위질할 때는 선을 먼저 그려요.
examples.en: When cutting cloth with scissors, I draw a line first.
I almost cut my hand while snipping with scissors.
If you cut slowly with scissors, it comes out neater.
Mom cut the meat up with scissors for me.

explain: 그냥 '자르다'보다 가위를 쓴다는 점이 분명해요. 식당에서 고기를 가위로 자를 때도 '가위질하다'를 써요. 대화에서는 '가위로 자르다'라고 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '자르다', it makes clear that scissors are used. It is also said when cutting meat with scissors at a restaurant. In conversation, '가위로 자르다' is more common.

examples.en: In the countryside, the fall harvest is in full swing now.
I went to Grandma's to help with the fall harvest.
It rained a lot this year, so the harvest got delayed.
When the harvest is over, the village holds a feast.
At harvest time the whole family works.
We rented machines to use for the harvest.

explain: 가을에 곡식이나 작물을 거두는 일을 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '추수'를 더 자주 쓰고, '가을걷이'는 순우리말이라 부드럽고 정겨운 느낌이에요. 시골 이야기나 글에서 잘 보여요.
explain_en: It means gathering grain and crops in autumn. The Sino-Korean '추수' is used more often, while '가을걷이' is a native Korean word with a softer, warmer feel. You see it in stories about the countryside.

examples.en: We harvest the rice in October.
Grandfather is harvesting beans in the field.

examples.ko: 비가 오기 전에 빨리 가을걷이해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to finish the harvest quickly before it rains.
The whole village gathered and harvested together.
After we finish the harvest, I'll share some rice.
This fall we plan to harvest the apples.

explain: 가을에 농작물을 거둔다는 뜻이라 봄이나 여름 수확에는 어색해요. 일상에서는 '수확하다'나 '추수하다'가 더 흔해요. 글이나 옛이야기 같은 분위기에서 쓰면 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Since it means gathering crops in autumn, it sounds odd for a spring or summer harvest. In daily speech '수확하다' or '추수하다' is more common. It fits a literary or old-tale mood well.

examples.en: We did a big cleaning to welcome autumn.
The department store is having a welcome-autumn sale.
I bought new bedding to welcome autumn.
Where shall we go for our autumn trip?
I organized my closet to get ready for autumn.
An autumn welcoming event takes place this weekend.

explain: '-맞이'는 어떤 때나 손님을 맞는 일을 뜻하고, 주로 앞 말에 계절이나 행사가 와요(새해맞이, 봄맞이). 가게의 광고 문구에서 '가을맞이 세일'처럼 자주 보여요.
explain_en: '-맞이' means welcoming a time or a guest, and it usually follows a season or event (새해맞이, 봄맞이). You often see it in store ads such as '가을맞이 세일'.

examples.ko: 가을볕이 툇마루에 길게 들어와서 고양이가 졸고 있어요.
examples.en: Autumn sunlight stretches across the porch and the cat is dozing.
I'm drying red peppers in the autumn sun.
The autumn sun is warm, so it's nice for a walk.
I read a book basking in the autumn sun.

examples.ko: 가을볕 아래 감이 빨갛게 익어 가요.
examples.en: Under the autumn sun the persimmons are ripening red.
Autumn sunshine is gentler than summer sun.

explain: '볕'은 따뜻하게 내리쬐는 햇빛을 말해서 '햇빛'보다 포근한 느낌이 있어요. 곡식이나 빨래를 말리는 장면에 특히 잘 어울려요. '가을볕에 그을리다'는 가을의 햇볕에 피부가 타는 모습이에요.
explain_en: '볕' means warm, shining sunlight, so it feels cozier than '햇빛'. It suits scenes of drying grain or laundry especially well. '가을볕에 그을리다' describes skin getting tanned by autumn sun.

examples.en: How much is the gym's membership fee?
You pay the joining fee only once at the start.
The joining fee is free this month.
If you pay the joining fee, we give you a coupon.
The club's joining fee is 10,000 won.
I'm hesitating to join because of the joining fee.

explain: 모임이나 회원제에 처음 들어갈 때 한 번 내는 돈이에요. 달마다 내는 '회비', '월 이용료'와 달라요. '가입비 면제'나 '가입비 무료'는 광고에서 자주 봐요.
explain_en: It is the one-time payment when you first join a club or membership. It differs from '회비' or '월 이용료', which are paid regularly. '가입비 면제' and '가입비 무료' are common in ads.

examples.en: Please write your name and contact number on the registration form.
I haven't submitted the gym registration form yet.
Where can I get the registration form?
Please fill out the form and show your ID.
A friend submitted the club registration form for me.
The registration form is too complicated.

explain: '가입서를 쓰다, 작성하다, 내다, 제출하다'처럼 짝이 되는 동사와 같이 외워 두면 좋아요. 같은 뜻으로 '가입 신청서'라고도 말해요. 가입하는 곳(동아리, 헬스장, 보험 등)은 앞에 붙여서 '동아리 가입서'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It helps to learn it with its usual verbs: '가입서를 쓰다, 작성하다, 내다, 제출하다'. People also say '가입 신청서' for the same thing. You can put the place you are joining in front, like '동아리 가입서' (club registration form).

examples.en: I had grilled flatfish for dinner.
A flatfish has a flat body.
I bought two flatfish at the market.
The flatfish is lying on the bottom.
Braised flatfish goes well with rice.
Mom made seaweed soup with flatfish for me.

explain: 몸이 납작하고 두 눈이 한쪽에 몰려 있는 바닷물고기예요. 비슷하게 생긴 '광어(넙치)'보다 크기가 작고 구이나 조림, 찌개로 많이 먹어요. 한국 식당 메뉴에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a flat sea fish with both eyes on one side. It is smaller than the similar-looking '광어' and is commonly eaten grilled, braised or in stew. You often see it on Korean restaurant menus.

examples.en: Family discord leaves a big wound on a child.
He went through a hard time because of trouble at home.
The cause of the family discord was a lack of conversation.
They decided to move because of family discord.
I comforted a friend who is going through family troubles.
Family discord should be solved by talking to each other.

explain: 부부나 가족 사이의 다툼과 갈등을 말하는 조금 딱딱한 표현이에요. 뉴스나 상담, 글에서 많이 쓰고, 보통 대화에서는 '집안 문제', '집에 일이 있다'처럼 돌려 말해요. '가정불화를 겪다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요.
explain_en: It is a somewhat formal term for quarrels and conflict between spouses or family members. It appears in news, counseling and writing, while in casual talk people say things like '집안 문제'. '가정불화를 겪다' is a common collocation.

examples.en: They sell household goods on this floor.
I bought the household goods I needed before moving.
Where is the household goods section?
Household goods are very cheap at this store.
If you order household goods all at once, delivery is free.
I looked at cleaning tools at the household goods shop.

explain: 집에서 쓰는 그릇, 청소 도구, 수건 같은 물건을 한꺼번에 부르는 말이에요. 마트나 쇼핑몰의 코너 이름으로 자주 보여요. 큰 가전제품은 보통 '가전'이라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It is a collective word for items used at home, such as dishes, cleaning tools and towels. You often see it as a section name in marts and shopping malls. Large appliances are usually called '가전' separately.

examples.en: My husband and I made our family plan together.
A couple should decide on family planning together.
There used to be many family planning campaigns.

examples.ko: 가족계획 때문에 아이를 늦게 가지기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to have kids later because of our family plans.
I got family planning counseling at the health center.
Our family plans differed, so we talked for a long time.

explain: 아이를 몇 명 낳을지, 언제 낳을지 계획하는 것을 말해요. 1960~80년대 정부 캠페인에서 많이 나온 말이라 지금은 조금 옛날 느낌이 있어요. 요즘 대화에서는 '아이 계획'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means planning how many children to have and when. The word was heavily used in government campaigns from the 1960s to the 1980s, so it now sounds a little dated. In modern conversation people also say '아이 계획'.

examples.en: Our company has a family-like atmosphere.

examples.ko: 가족적인 식당이라 편하게 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: It's a homey restaurant, so you can eat comfortably.
I like the family-like team culture.

examples.ko: 사장님이 가족적인 성격이라 직원들을 잘 챙겨요.
examples.en: The boss has a warm, family-minded nature and looks after the staff.
It felt like family, so it wasn't awkward from the start.
It's a family-style gathering, so you can bring your child.

explain: '가족 같은'이라는 따뜻하고 친한 분위기를 말해요. 보통 '가족적인'이나 '가족적이다' 형태로 써요. 회사 광고에서는 좋은 뜻이지만 사생활이 없다는 불평으로도 쓰일 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a warm, close, family-like atmosphere. It is usually used as '가족적인' or '가족적이다'. In company ads it is a plus, but it can also hint at a complaint about no personal boundaries.

examples.en: The leather strap of my watch snapped.
I tied up the bag with a leather strap.
I made a leather strap bracelet myself.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 가죽끈이 길어서 매기 편해요.
examples.en: This bag has a long leather strap, so it's easy to carry.
A leather strap softens as you use it for a long time.
I attached the key to a leather strap and hung it on my neck.

explain: 가죽으로 만든 끈이라서 줄이나 실보다 튼튼하고 고급스러운 느낌이 있어요. 시계, 가방, 목걸이, 팔찌에 자주 써요. '길이 들다'는 쓸수록 부드러워진다는 뜻으로 가죽 제품에 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Being made of leather, it feels sturdier and more upscale than ordinary string. It is often used on watches, bags, necklaces and bracelets. '길이 들다' means to become softer with use and is often said about leather goods.

examples.en: At the market there are all kinds of things.
He dodged out, giving every kind of excuse.
Everyone has their own different worries.

examples.ko: 가지가지 하는 아이라서 늘 정신이 없어요.
examples.en: That kid does one thing after another, so it's always hectic.
The flowers bloomed in a variety of colors.
I tried everything under the sun, but it was useless.

explain: 종류가 여러 가지라는 뜻이지만 '가지가지 하네'처럼 말하면 어이없고 못마땅한 느낌이 되기도 해요. 좋은 뜻으로 여러 종류를 말할 때는 '여러 가지'가 더 무난해요. 말투와 상황을 보고 써야 해요.
explain_en: It means many kinds, but a phrase like '가지가지 하네' carries a feeling of exasperation or disapproval. For a neutral, positive meaning of many kinds, '여러 가지' is safer. Watch the tone and situation.

examples.en: People's outfits in the park are all different.
Balloons of every color floated up into the sky.
The students' dreams are all different, which is interesting.
All sorts of reactions came out.
The umbrellas opened in every color.
In autumn, the mountain's leaves are of every color.

explain: 색깔뿐 아니라 모양, 생각, 반응이 각각 다를 때도 써요. '가지가지'는 종류가 많은 걸, '가지각색'은 서로 다르게 다양한 걸 강조해요. '가지각색이다', '가지각색의'처럼 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It covers not only colors but also shapes, opinions and reactions that all differ. '가지가지' stresses many kinds, while '가지각색' stresses that each is different. It is typically said as '가지각색이다' or '가지각색의'.

examples.en: I was surprised at how many side dishes there were.
We decided to reduce the number of menu items.
There aren't many kinds, but all of them taste good.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 상품 가짓수가 정말 많아요.
examples.en: This store has a really wide variety of products.
Quality matters more than the number of kinds.
If there are too many kinds, it's hard to choose.

explain: 물건이나 일이 몇 종류인지를 가리켜요. 몇 개인지를 세는 '개수'와 달리 종류의 수를 말해요. '반찬 가짓수', '메뉴 가짓수'처럼 음식 이야기에서 특히 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to how many kinds of things or items there are. Unlike '개수', which counts pieces, it counts types. It appears especially in food contexts like '반찬 가짓수' and '메뉴 가짓수'.

examples.en: The cow has a fever, so I called the veterinary clinic.
The vet clinic in our neighborhood is open on Sundays too.
The vet from the animal hospital came to the farm in person.
The pig got hurt, so we moved it to the animal hospital.
There aren't many livestock clinics in the countryside.

examples.ko: 가축병원에서 주사를 맞고 나니 송아지가 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: After getting a shot at the vet, the calf got better.

explain: 소, 돼지, 닭 같은 가축을 치료하는 곳이라는 느낌이 강해요. 강아지나 고양이를 데려가는 곳은 보통 '동물병원'이라고 말해요. 사람이 가는 곳은 그냥 '병원'이고, 치료하는 사람은 '수의사'예요.
explain_en: This word strongly suggests a place that treats livestock such as cows, pigs, and chickens. For taking a dog or cat, people usually say '동물병원'. A place for people is just '병원', and the person who treats animals is a '수의사' (vet).

examples.en: I bought a newspaper at the stand in the subway station.
A street stall opens every morning.
Fruit is piled high on the stall.
The woman at the stand gave me my change.
The socks sold at the stall are cheap.
Once the stalls are cleared away, the street gets wide.

explain: 길이나 역 앞에 임시로 놓고 물건을 파는 작은 판매대예요. 신문, 과일, 양말, 액세서리를 팔 때가 많아요. 가게 안의 '진열대'와 달리 밖에 있는 간이 판매대를 말해요.
explain_en: It is a small temporary sales stand set up on a street or in front of a station. It often sells newspapers, fruit, socks or accessories. Unlike a '진열대' (display shelf) inside a shop, it is an outdoor makeshift stand.

examples.en: A prism has a polygon as its base.
A triangular prism and a rectangular prism are both prisms.
We drew a prism in math class.
The side faces of a prism are rectangles.
This box is shaped like a prism.
How are a prism and a cylinder different?

explain: 수학에서 위아래 밑면이 같은 다각형인 기둥 모양 입체도형이에요. 밑면이 동그란 '원기둥', 뾰족한 '각뿔'과 같이 배워요. 일상에서는 '네모난 기둥'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: In math it is a solid whose top and bottom bases are identical polygons. It is learned alongside the round-based '원기둥' (cylinder) and the pointed '각뿔' (pyramid). In daily life people say things like '네모난 기둥'.

examples.en: I measured the size of the angle with a protractor.
I forgot to bring my protractor.
The markings on this protractor are easy to see.
Line up the center of the protractor with the vertex.
I didn't have a protractor, so I borrowed one from a friend.

examples.ko: 각도기에는 안쪽 눈금과 바깥쪽 눈금이 있어요.
examples.en: A protractor has an inner scale and an outer scale.

explain: 각도를 재는 반원 모양의 도구로, 초등 수학 시간에 처음 써 봐요. '자'와 함께 학용품으로 같이 사는 경우가 많아요. 영어 'protractor'와 같고 '각도를 재다'와 같이 말해요.
explain_en: It is the half-circle tool for measuring angles, first used in elementary school math. It is often bought together with a ruler as school supplies. It pairs with the verb phrase '각도를 재다'.

examples.en: A pyramid has a pointed top.
The side faces of a square pyramid are triangles.
How many vertices does a pyramid have?

examples.ko: 각뿔 중에서 이집트의 피라미드는 밑면이 사각형이에요.
examples.en: Among pyramids, the Egyptian ones have a square base.
I tried folding a pyramid out of paper.
Compare a pyramid and a prism.

explain: 밑면이 다각형이고 옆면이 삼각형으로 모여 한 점에서 만나는 입체도형이에요. '피라미드'는 일상 단어이고 '각뿔'은 수학 용어예요. 밑면이 삼각형이면 삼각뿔, 사각형이면 사각뿔이에요.
explain_en: It is a solid with a polygon base and triangular sides that meet at one point. '피라미드' is the everyday word, while '각뿔' is the math term. A triangle base gives a 삼각뿔 and a square base gives a 사각뿔.

examples.en: I put one sugar cube into my coffee.
A sugar cube dissolves quickly in hot water.
The café gave me sugar cubes separately.
Two sugar cubes are sweet enough.
I tried feeding a sugar cube to a horse.
Sugar cubes are square, so they are easy to use.

explain: 네모나게 굳힌 설탕 덩어리예요. 커피나 차에 넣을 때 많이 쓰고, 한 개 두 개로 세요. 가루인 '설탕'보다 양을 맞추기 쉬워요.
explain_en: It is sugar pressed into small squares. It is commonly used in coffee or tea and counted as one, two and so on. It is easier to measure than granulated '설탕'.

examples.en: I take care of my father at the hospital every day.
I took leave from work to look after my mother.
It isn't easy for family to nurse a patient directly.
We are looking for someone to care for the patient.
My older brother nursed Grandma all night.
I'm truly grateful to the person who cares for the patient.

explain: 아픈 사람 곁에서 먹이고 씻기고 돌보는 일을 말해요. 의사나 간호사의 치료인 '치료하다'와 달리 생활을 도와주는 돌봄이에요. '간병인', '간병비'처럼 사람이나 돈 이야기에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means staying beside a sick person to feed, wash and look after them. Unlike '치료하다', the treatment by doctors and nurses, it is daily-life caregiving. It also appears in related words like '간병인' (caregiver) and '간병비' (care costs).

examples.en: I ate ramyeon at the little snack bar in front of the park.
It's a simple eatery, so there aren't many menu items.
The snack bar at the rest area is crowded at lunchtime.

examples.ko: 간이식당에서 간단히 김밥 한 줄 먹을까요?
examples.en: Shall we have a roll of gimbap at the snack bar?
A new simple eatery opened next to the construction site.
For a simple eatery, the food is pretty good.

explain: 격식을 갖춘 식당이 아니라 간단히 먹을 수 있는 작고 소박한 가게를 말해요. 휴게소, 공원, 학교 근처 같은 곳에서 볼 수 있는 곳이에요. 가게 이름으로는 잘 안 쓰고, 어떤 종류의 가게인지 설명할 때 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a small, simple place to grab a quick meal rather than a formal restaurant, like ones near rest stops, parks, or schools. It is rarely used as a shop's actual name; people use it to describe what kind of place it is.

examples.en: Value-added tax is a typical indirect tax.
Indirect taxes are included in the price of goods.
The share of indirect taxes is rising.
I didn't know that consumers pay indirect taxes.
Indirect taxes apply the same regardless of income.
In social studies we learned about direct and indirect taxes.

explain: 물건을 살 때 값에 섞여 내는 세금이라서, 소득에서 바로 내는 '직접세'와 짝으로 배워요. 대표적인 예가 부가가치세예요. 뉴스나 경제 수업에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a tax built into the price when you buy something, so it is learned as a pair with '직접세' (direct tax), which is paid straight from income. VAT is the typical example. It often appears in the news and economics classes.

examples.ko: 간접흡연은 아이들 건강에 특히 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Second-hand smoke is especially bad for children's health.
I want to avoid second-hand smoke at restaurants.
I'm worried about second-hand smoke because of my family.

examples.ko: 간접흡연 피해를 줄이려고 환기를 자주 해요.
examples.en: I ventilate often to reduce the harm of second-hand smoke.
Some people cough because of second-hand smoke.
You have to be careful about second-hand smoke at bus stops too.

explain: 내가 피우지 않아도 다른 사람의 연기를 마시게 되는 것을 말하고, 반대말은 '직접흡연'이에요. '간접흡연 피해', '간접흡연에 노출되다'처럼 건강 이야기나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 발음은 [간저프변]으로 소리 나요.
explain_en: It describes breathing in someone else's smoke even though you don't smoke yourself, and its opposite is '직접흡연' (direct smoking). It often appears in health talk and news in phrases like '간접흡연 피해' and '간접흡연에 노출되다'. It is pronounced [간저프변].

examples.en: I am very ticklish.
Please don't tickle the soles of my feet.
I couldn't stop laughing because of the tickling.
The baby giggles at the tickle.
I felt a tickle on my neck and turned around.
My older sister isn't ticklish at all.

explain: '간지럼을 타다'는 쉽게 간지러움을 느낀다는 뜻이고, '간지럼을 태우다'는 남을 간지럽게 하는 뜻이라서 구분해야 해요. '간지러움'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰지만 대화에서는 '간지럼'이 더 흔해요.
explain_en: Keep '간지럼을 타다' (to be ticklish) apart from '간지럼을 태우다' (to tickle someone). '간지러움' has the same meaning, but '간지럼' is more common in conversation.

examples.en: My younger sibling keeps tickling the soles of my feet.
If you tickle the baby, he laughs a lot.
Don't tickle me with a feather!
A friend tickled my side and I was startled.
I tickled the puppy's belly and it loved it.
My hair tickled my nose and I sneezed.

explain: '간지럽다'는 내 몸이 간지러운 상태이고, '간지럽히다'는 남(또는 물건)이 간지럽게 만든다는 뜻이라 '~을/를' 목적어가 꼭 필요해요. '간질이다'도 비슷하게 쓸 수 있어요. 활용은 '간지럽혀요, 간지럽혔어요'처럼 'ㅂ'이 그대로 남아요.
explain_en: '간지럽다' describes your own body feeling ticklish or itchy, while '간지럽히다' means someone or something makes it so, so it needs an object with '을/를'. '간질이다' can be used in a similar way. It conjugates as '간지럽혀요, 간지럽혔어요', keeping the 'ㅂ'.

examples.en: My sister tickled my side.
If you tickle the child, he giggles.
Please don't tickle my nose with a feather.
The breeze gently tickles my face.
The puppy tickled my hand with its paw.
That song gives a feeling that tickles the heart.

explain: 남의 몸을 살살 건드려 간지럽게 한다는 뜻이에요. '간질이다'는 어간이 '간질이'로 끝나서 '간질여요'가 돼요. 바람이나 감정이 부드럽게 건드린다는 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It means lightly touching someone's body so it feels ticklish. The stem ends in '간질이', which gives '간질여요'. It is also used figuratively for a breeze or a feeling that gently stirs something.

examples.en: On busy days I eat convenience food for dinner.
The convenience store's ready meals have become really varied.
You just heat the convenience food in the microwave.
I live alone, so I often buy ready meals.
The ready-meal market is growing every year.

examples.ko: 이 간편식은 맛도 괜찮고 값도 싸요.
examples.en: This ready meal tastes decent and is cheap too.

explain: 도시락, 즉석밥, 냉동식품처럼 빠르고 쉽게 먹을 수 있게 만든 음식이에요. 뉴스에서는 '간편식 시장'처럼 소비 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 일상에서는 '즉석식품', '편의점 도시락'처럼 구체적으로 말해요.
explain_en: It covers foods made to be eaten quickly and easily, such as lunch boxes, instant rice and frozen food. In the news it appears in consumer talk such as '간편식 시장'. In daily speech people are more specific, saying '즉석식품' or '편의점 도시락'.

examples.en: A person in a nurse uniform came into the ward.
The new nurse uniform is more comfortable than the old one.
The nurse uniforms at our hospital are light green.
I'd like to change my nurse uniform size.
As soon as I got to work, I changed into my nurse uniform.
I went to lunch in my nurse uniform.

explain: 간호사가 일할 때 입는 옷이고, '간호사복'이라고도 해요. 환자가 입는 옷은 '환자복'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 옷을 입을 때는 '입다', 다른 옷으로 바꿀 때는 '갈아입다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is the clothing a nurse wears at work, and it is also called '간호사복'. What a patient wears is '환자복', so the two are different. Use '입다' to wear it and '갈아입다' to change into it.

examples.en: I was in a hurry, so I scrawled the note.
If you scribble, you can't read it later.
The doctor scribbled the prescription.
I ran short on exam time and scrawled my answers.
He scrawled his name on the board and left.

examples.ko: 숙제를 갈겨쓰지 말고 또박또박 써 오세요.
examples.en: Don't scribble your homework; write it neatly.

explain: 글씨를 천천히 쓰지 않고 마구 빠르게 쓴다는 뜻이에요. 반대로 한 글자씩 정성 들여 쓰는 건 '또박또박 쓰다'라고 해요. 비슷한 말로 '휘갈기다', '날려 쓰다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It means writing fast and carelessly instead of slowly. The opposite, writing each letter carefully, is '또박또박 쓰다'. Similar words include '휘갈기다' and '날려 쓰다'.

examples.en: The autumn reed field is pretty, swaying in the wind.
I went to see the reed fields at Suncheon Bay.
A path runs through the reed field.
Birds flew up from the reed field.
The sunset settled over the reed field.
The reed field turned golden.

explain: 강이나 바닷가 습지에 갈대가 넓게 자란 곳이에요. 가을에 바람에 흔들리는 풍경으로 사진을 찍으러 많이 가요. 갈대는 바람에 잘 흔들려서 '갈대 같은 마음'처럼 마음이 잘 변한다는 비유로도 말해요.
explain_en: It is a wide area where reeds grow in wetlands near rivers or the sea. Many people go to take photos of it swaying in the autumn wind. Because reeds sway easily, '갈대 같은 마음' is a metaphor for a fickle heart.

examples.en: In autumn the reed grove sways in a silvery color.
A walking path runs through the reeds.
Birds were hiding in the reed thicket.
When the wind blew, the reed bed made a rustling sound.
Do you want to go see the reed field this weekend?
I took a lot of photos next to the reed field.

explain: 갈대가 빽빽하게 자란 곳을 '숲'이라고 부르는 말이에요. 가을 풍경이나 산책, 사진 이야기에서 자주 나오고, 비슷한 풍경으로 '억새밭'도 있어요. 발음은 [갈때숩]으로 소리 나요.
explain_en: It calls a dense stand of reeds a 'forest' (숲). It often comes up when talking about autumn scenery, walks, and photos, and '억새밭' (a field of silvergrass) is a similar kind of scene. It is pronounced [갈때숩].

examples.en: I quickly pulled the fighting kids apart.
The war tore the family apart.
Please split the cake in half.
Someone is trying to come between us.
A river divides the village into two.
A money problem drove the two friends apart.

explain: 붙어 있거나 가까운 것을 둘로 나누어 떨어뜨린다는 뜻이에요. 물건을 나눌 때뿐 아니라 사람 사이를 멀어지게 할 때도 써요. 사람 관계에서는 '사이를 갈라놓다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means separating things that were joined or close into two parts. It works for dividing objects and also for driving people apart. For relationships, '사이를 갈라놓다' is the natural phrase.

examples.en: I fell and my ribs hurt so much.
I got an X-ray at the hospital to see if my rib was broken.
I lost weight, so my ribs show.

examples.ko: 숨을 쉴 때마다 갈빗대 쪽이 쑤셔요.
examples.en: My rib area aches every time I breathe.
The doctor pressed on my ribs and asked questions.
Please press the area below your ribs with your hand.

explain: 몸의 가슴을 둘러싼 뼈를 말하고, '갈비뼈'라고도 해요. 먹는 '갈비'(고기)와 헷갈리지 않게, 몸 이야기에서는 '갈빗대'나 '갈비뼈'를 써요. 발음은 [갈빋때]로 소리 나요.
explain_en: It means the bones that surround the chest, and it is also called '갈비뼈'. Don't confuse it with '갈비', the meat you eat; in talk about the body, use '갈빗대' or '갈비뼈'. It is pronounced [갈빋때].
